name: Graphify — 74.8K Stars; /graphify Turns Any Codebase Into a Queryable Knowledge Graph (71.5x Token Savings)
hook: YC S26 company Graphify has reached 74.8K stars with a skill that parses your entire codebase (code, SQL schemas, R scripts, shell scripts, docs, PDFs, images, videos) into a local queryable knowledge graph — then Claude queries the graph instead of re-reading files. Code is parsed locally via tree-sitter (no API calls); docs and media route through the session model. Benchmark: for a large mixed code-and-paper corpus, average query cost was 1.7K tokens vs. 123K naive — a 71.5x reduction. Charlie Automates published a setup guide this week pairing Graphify with Obsidian for cross-project persistent memory. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and 15+ other agents. MIT licensed.

name: Claude Code Routines — Official Cloud-Scheduled Agents; Cron, API Trigger, and GitHub Events
hook: Claude Code Routines is the official Anthropic system for putting agents on autopilot — define a prompt once, wire up a trigger, and Claude Code runs autonomously on Anthropic-managed cloud infrastructure (4 vCPUs, 16GB RAM per agent) against any connected GitHub repo whenever the trigger fires. Three trigger types: Schedule (any cron cadence or one-off timestamp), API (HTTP POST to a per-routine endpoint with bearer-token auth), and GitHub event (PR opened, release created, push to branch). Managed at claude.ai/code/routines or via /schedule. Available on Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise. This week's blog spotlight — a dev.to post titled 'Put Your AI Agent on Autopilot,' a sabrina.dev deep-dive on loop engineering with /goal + routines, and a MindStudio explainer — is driving renewed adoption awareness. No laptop, no .env files, no token-limit exposure.

name: ponytail — 73.7K Stars; 7-Rung Minimalism Ladder That Cuts Code Output 54% and Tokens 22%
hook: ponytail hit 44K stars in the 9 days after its June 12 launch and is now at 73.7K — the fastest-growing Claude Code plugin of June 2026. It injects a mandatory 7-rung minimalism ladder before Claude writes any code: Does it need to exist? Already in codebase? In stdlib? Native platform feature? Existing dependency? One-liner? Only then: minimum code. Benchmarks on a real FastAPI + React repo across 12 tasks show 54% fewer lines, 22% fewer tokens, 20% lower cost, 27% faster completion. v4.8.4 (June 29) added Hermes support. Works with Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode, and Gemini CLI.

name: headroom v0.30.0 — 56.4K Stars; 60-95% Token Reduction via SmartCrusher, CodeCompressor, and Kompress-v2
hook: headroom v0.30.0 (July 3, their 160th release) compresses tool outputs, logs, files, and RAG chunks 60-95% before they reach the LLM using three purpose-built engines: SmartCrusher (JSON), CodeCompressor (AST-aware), and Kompress-v2-base (general text). Compression is reversible — originals cached locally for on-demand retrieval. Three deployment modes: Python library, transparent proxy (headroom wrap claude), or MCP server. v0.30.0 adds cross-agent memory dedup so Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex share compressed context without re-processing the same files. 56.4K stars. LiteLLM integrated headroom natively in June.

name: PMB (oleksiijko) — Local-First Persistent Project Memory MCP; 35ms Warm Recall, No Cloud
hook: PMB (project memory base) solves the cold-start problem: every new Claude Code session wastes minutes re-explaining decisions already made and why the architecture looks the way it does. v1.2.2 stores them in a local SQLite database with hybrid three-layer retrieval — BM25 keyword + vector semantic + entity graph — with ~35ms warm recall. No cloud, no API key on the read path. Connects via `pmb connect claude-code` which writes the MCP config automatically; also works with Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, and Zed. Surfaced via 'Show HN: Recall – Local project memory for Claude Code.'
install: pip install pmb-ai && pmb setup && pmb connect claude-code
